correctness.rationale: For odd N, the cyclic quadratic Gauss sum at slope difference d and modulation difference l vanishes unless gcd(d,N)|l, otherwise its squared modulus is N*gcd(d,N). Summing fourth powers across the N² modulation pairs gives precisely gcd(d,N), while same-slope bases contribute N each. The identity gcd(d,N)=sum_{m|gcd(d,N)}phi(m) transforms the potential into a positive combination of class-pair counts mod every divisor m. Integer exchange lowers a collision sum unless the counts are balanced; consecutive slope intervals balance all divisors simultaneously. The proof covers every N>=3 odd and 1<=r<=N, including singleton/full families. Exhaustive 35490 finite subsets, randomized integer identities and direct Gauss calculations independently support, but do not replace, that analytic argument.

value.rationale: Approximate mutual unbiasedness and projective-design energy are canonical metrics for choosing several bases. For odd composite dimensions, quadratic-chirp cross correlations are arithmetic and far from uniformly unbiased. The theorem gives the exact best second frame potential for every cardinality, a closed divisor-weighted formula, the complete set of minimizers and a quantitative nonnegative defect. This is structural constrained-basis design rather than a single arbitrary finite example; the smallest-prime factor marks precisely where ideal mutual-unbiased energy first becomes impossible within this family.
